title: Fragmented KV sharding protocol for pipeline-aware multi-GPU placement
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: As we scale inference across pipeline and tensor parallel ranks, the KV cache size grows and naive full-replication or coarse striping either wastes GPU memory or incurs high cross-GPU transfer overhead during generation. Continuous batching makes memory pressure and access patterns non-uniform across timesteps: early tokens access different KV slices than late tokens, and micro-batches interleave pipeline stages.

Goal: Implement a fragmented sharding protocol that places KV fragments (short-lived, context-aligned slices) on GPUs according to pipeline stage ownership and token hotness, minimizing cross-GPU hops for the common-case streaming workload while bounding worst-case latency. The protocol must interoperate with continuous batching and tensor-parallel layouts, support fast epoch-based remapping, and allow a graceful fallback to replica or stripe modes when skew or failures occur.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by infra and serving runtime (links in comments)
Prototype implemented in serving runtime that can run with 2-8 GPUs and both pipeline/tensor parallel configs
Benchmarks showing >=20% reduction in cross-GPU KV transfer volume on representative streaming workloads compared to baseline full-replication
p99 generation latency no worse than baseline +5ms for typical prompt lengths, and improved p50/p90 under memory-constrained scenarios
Fallback path via full-replication mode and safety timeouts implemented and tested
Observability hooks: metrics for cross_gpu_bytes, fragment_migrations, fragment_hit_rate, and a trace for remap events
decision_log: 2026-02-18: Chose fragment (sub-slab) abstraction over slab to allow fine-grained eviction and per-fragment replication policies
2026-02-22: Use epoch-based lock-free remapping table (single writer per coordinator) to avoid expensive distributed locks during continuous batching
2026-03-01: Prioritize placement by pipeline stage ownership; replicate hot fragments to next-stage GPU if cross-stage access rate > threshold
2026-03-05: Opted for predictive prefetching using token-horizon heuristics collected from continuous-batching traces rather than aggressive eager replication
2026-03-08: Implemented asymmetric replication: small hot fragments are 2-way replicated, large cold fragments remain single-shard to conserve memory
implementation_notes:
Key components in prototype: (1) fragment descriptor table (compact, RDMA-friendly) maintained by coordinator; (2) per-rank fragment cache with LRU+TTL tuned to token horizon; (3) remap fast-path: if fragment present locally, serve; else check 1-hop neighbor (pipeline successor/predecessor) before coordinator RPC; (4) eviction policy that considers fragment size, access frequency, and upcoming prefetch hints. Interaction with tensor-parallel: store intra-tensor PV (partial values) contiguously so tensor-parallel reduce steps don't require extra PCIe hops.

Trade-offs considered: aggressive replication lowers hop latency but increases memory footprint; fine-grained fragments reduce transfer bytes but increase descriptor bookkeeping overhead; epoch remap simplifies concurrency at cost of slightly stale placement info during in-flight micro-batches.
benchmarks_summary: Prototype on 4xA100 cluster with a synthetic streaming workload (avg context 1.2k tokens, steady-state micro-batch size 8): cross-GPU KV bytes reduced by 34% vs full-replication baseline, tokens/sec improved by 9%, p99 latency improved by 12% under memory-constrained run (warm cache). Worst-case tail when forced remap occurred saw +18ms due to coordinator roundtrip; mitigated by local fallback to neighbor replica. Detailed csv and graphs in benchmark PR.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Coordinator becomes bottleneck for remap ops under highly skewed micro-batches. Mitigation: batch remap updates, use hierarchical coordinators per rack, and fall back to conservative replica mode when coordinator lag detected.

Risk: Fragment bookkeeping grows with sequence length and many concurrent requests. Mitigation: compact fragment ids, GC short-lived fragments aggressively, and cap descriptor table size with sampling eviction.

Risk: Interference with tensor-parallel reductions causing extra synchronization. Mitigation: align fragment layout to tensor shard boundaries and add a lightweight barrier in the fast-path to touch local shards first.
Risk: Debuggability of remap races under continuous batching. Mitigation: add trace span for each remap decision and rich metrics for fragment hits/misses by micro-batch id.
